title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building, by hand, the one-dimensional case of his 'tame topology' (Esquisse d'un programme, §5) in the 4th version of 'Analysis situs'. The ambient object is an ordered line L. M_1 is the set of segments S_{a,b}. A 'préfigure' is a finite combinatorial cell-like object on L: a set of vertices together with a set of 1-cells, where vertices may be missing and 1-cells may be subdivided.

The proposition begun on p.114 classifies préfigures by explicit data.

Data 1: a figure Ψ, a disjoint union of segments X_i = S_{a_i,b_i}. It is given equivalently by a strictly increasing sequence a_1<b_1<...<a_n<b_n. Its boundary is ∂Ψ = {a_i, b_i}.

Data 2: a finite 'drapeau' Δ ∈ Drap*(L), i.e. a finite set of points of L, with Δ ⊃ ∂Ψ.

On this page Δ is cut into three disjoint pieces:
- Δ_int = Δ ∩ Omb°(Ψ_1), the points of Δ lying in the open interior ('open shadow') of some segment S_{a_i,b_i}. This is automatically contained in Δ \ ∂Ψ.
- Δ_is = (Δ \ ∂Ψ) \ Δ_int, the points of Δ outside Ψ (isolated vertices).
- ∂Ψ itself.
So Δ = Δ_is ⊔ Δ_int ⊔ ∂Ψ.

Further data:
- A subset Δ_loc ⊂ Δ_int. Its complement Δ_red = Δ_int \ Δ_loc gives Δ_int = Δ_loc ⊔ Δ_red.
- A subset ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ, the 'proper' boundary vertices.

To these data he associates the préfigure 𝔓:
- Vertex set 𝔓_0 = ∂_0 (proper boundary vertices) ∪ Δ_red (redundant vertices, i.e. vertices subdividing a segment) ∪ Δ_is (isolated vertices).
- Edge set 𝔓_1 = the interstitial intervals of Δ (the elements of 𝔓_Δ ∩ M_1) that lie in Omb(Ψ).

Thus the points of Δ_loc and of ∂Ψ \ ∂_0 are cut points of the edges that are not vertices: improper boundary, open ends.

The next page checks that δΦ = Δ, ∂Φ = ∂Ψ, ∂_0Φ = ∂_0, Φ_red = Δ_red, and so on. It concludes that a préfigure is uniquely determined by these data. The irredundant ones (Δ_red = ∅, i.e. Δ_loc = Δ ∩ Omb°(Ψ_1)) correspond to triples ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ ⊂ Δ.

In modern terms, this is a bookkeeping classification of finite, stratified, possibly non-closed 1-dimensional cell structures on a line: finite unions of points and of open, half-open or closed intervals, with marked subdivision points.
errors: No mathematical error. The inclusion Δ_int ⊂ Δ \ ∂Ψ is correct because the open shadow excludes the endpoints, and the decompositions are tautologically disjoint.

Minor notational looseness: Omb°(Ψ_1) is used here, while the next page writes Omb°(Ψ) = ∪ Omb°(Ψ_i). The numbering of the data items (1°/2°/3°/4°) is inconsistent across pp.114–116 because of corrections.

ideas.what: Classification of 1-dimensional 'préfigures' on an ordered line by combinatorial data (segments, a finite flag containing their endpoints, a choice of proper boundary points, and a choice of redundant versus localized subdivision points)
ideas.modern_name: Cell decomposition / stratification of definable subsets of a line (1-dim o-minimal cell decomposition; finite semi-open cell complexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s); tame topology program: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of 'topologie modérée' appears, in Esquisse d'un programme §5; these combinatorial details are unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Distinguishing proper and improper boundary vertices, and redundant and isolated vertices, of a figure
ideas.modern_name: Closed vs. open ends of cells; refinement or subdivision of a stratification

deep.surprise_reason: This is elementary bookkeeping for the one-dimensional case of a tame-topology foundation. It is correct and routine, and it contains nothing a specialist in o-minimal or tame topology would find new. Its interest is only as documentation of how Grothendieck set up the combinatorics of 'préfigures'.
transcription_corrections: 'intérieurs ... des intervalles ∫_{a_i,b_i}' should read 'intérieurs aux intervalles S_{a_i,b_i}'. The symbol is Grothendieck's segment notation S, not an integral sign.
'on associe le préphygone [?]' should read 'on associe la préfigure 𝔓'.
The first top-line attempt reads 'Δ_is = Δ \ Δ ∩ Omb°(Ψ_1)', with the whole line struck through and Δ ∩ Omb°(Ψ_1) underbraced as Δ_int.

The item numbering is uncertain. The image shows an overwritten numeral before 'Une partie Δ_loc' (likely 3° rewritten), and '2°)' written over a struck '3' before 'Une partie ∂_0'. Given p.116's 'données 1°) 2°) 3°) 4°)', these are probably items 3° and 4° of the proposition.
The annotations under 𝔓_0 read 'sommets bord propres' and 'sommets redondants'. The annotation under 𝔓_Δ ∩ M_1 reads 'intervalles interstitiels de Δ'.
